Short answer: the retrieval architecture for a healthcare appointment assistant should keep the booking database authoritative, retain a replayable change log beside a rebuildable index, and degrade to constrained database lookup rather than serve a slot whose freshness cannot be proved.
For a healthcare appointment assistant, the expensive term is rarely the few sentences returned to a model. It is the retained, duplicated state: embeddings, index replicas, document payloads, change history, snapshots, and the temporary overlap required during a rebuild. Before choosing a retrieval engine, write the bill as source records + change log + active index + rebuild index + backups. If the active index contains every historical slot and every copy of unchanged provider text, retention dominates …

MeshXFS is a new open-source file system that lets several Linux servers share one disk at the same time. It was built by modifying XFS with AI coding agents, Phoronix reported on October 17, 2026. The project's repository says no human wrote, hand-edited or reviewed its clustering code line by line. That makes it one of the clearest tests yet of AI-written code in a place where a bug can destroy data.
XFS is a mature file system that ships in the Linux kernel. A normal XFS volume can be mounted by only one machine at a time. A clustered file system lets several machines mount the same shared disk and write to it together, which is common in virtualization clusters.
Claude Opus, running as an autonomous coding agent in Anthropic's Claude Code, "wrote a large share" of the code, according t…
articles.title: MeshXFS: an AI-written clustered file system built on XFS

The visits table is the central fact table: each row records one patient visit, including the doctor, department, ward, diagnosis, procedure, admission type, length of stay, bill amount, payment method, and satisfaction score. [file:1]
A window function performs a calculation across a set of related rows—called a window—without collapsing those rows into one output row. This differs from GROUP BY, which returns one row per group. Window functions are useful in a hospital setting when you need to retain individual visit details while also showing department totals, rankings, running totals, or comparisons with previous visits.
